# SQLBraid

> SQL-first TypeScript data access. Keep ordinary SQL while SQLBraid provides explicit result contracts, safe value binding, structural SQL helpers, runtime scope, adapters, metadata, code generation, and editor/agent tooling.

This index belongs to the release 1.0.0 snapshot at https://clickin.github.io/SQLBraid/v/1.0.0/. Every documentation link below returns raw Markdown from the same snapshot.

Assume ordinary SQL knowledge. Use these documents for SQLBraid-specific APIs, guarantees, limits, and database/driver behavior rather than generic SQL syntax.

## Start here
- [SQLBraid](https://clickin.github.io/SQLBraid/v/1.0.0/index.md): Write SQL. Keep TypeScript. Skip the query-builder translation layer.
- [SQL tags and result kinds](https://clickin.github.io/SQLBraid/v/1.0.0/concepts/sql-tags.md): Declare what a SQLBraid statement returns without hiding the SQL.
- [Safe binds](https://clickin.github.io/SQLBraid/v/1.0.0/concepts/safe-binds.md): Keep values as driver parameters and make structural SQL explicit.
- [Structural SQL fragments](https://clickin.github.io/SQLBraid/v/1.0.0/concepts/structural-fragments.md): Make identifiers, lists, joins, and trusted raw SQL visible in the API.
- [Transactions and savepoints](https://clickin.github.io/SQLBraid/v/1.0.0/runtime/transactions.md): Pin one physical connection and make transaction scope explicit.
- [Portable agent skill](https://clickin.github.io/SQLBraid/v/1.0.0/agents/skill.md): Install SQLBraid's application-development guidance in compatible coding agents.

## Getting started
- [MariaDB quickstart](https://clickin.github.io/SQLBraid/v/1.0.0/getting-started/mariadb.md): Connect SQLBraid to MariaDB Connector/Node.js while keeping MariaDB syntax explicit.
- [SQL Server quickstart](https://clickin.github.io/SQLBraid/v/1.0.0/getting-started/mssql.md): Connect SQLBraid to Tedious with deterministic SQL Server parameter hints.
- [MySQL quickstart](https://clickin.github.io/SQLBraid/v/1.0.0/getting-started/mysql.md): Connect SQLBraid to mysql2 with either a direct connection or an explicit pool.
- [Oracle quickstart](https://clickin.github.io/SQLBraid/v/1.0.0/getting-started/oracle.md): Connect SQLBraid to node-oracledb in Thin mode with explicit Oracle parameter hints.
- [PostgreSQL quickstart](https://clickin.github.io/SQLBraid/v/1.0.0/getting-started/postgres.md): Connect SQLBraid to pg with either a direct client or an explicit pool.
- [Five-minute SQLite quickstart](https://clickin.github.io/SQLBraid/v/1.0.0/getting-started/sqlite.md): Run your first SQLBraid query with Node's built-in SQLite driver.
- [Browser SQLite and D1](https://clickin.github.io/SQLBraid/v/1.0.0/getting-started/sqlite-browser.md): Use the SQLite WASM and Cloudflare D1 adapters without inventing a browser pool or cursor.
- [Vite integration](https://clickin.github.io/SQLBraid/v/1.0.0/getting-started/vite.md): Lower SQLBraid guarded templates in Vite 8 without taking over TypeScript or TSX transforms.

## Core concepts
- [Homogeneous bulk DML](https://clickin.github.io/SQLBraid/v/1.0.0/concepts/bulk.md): Execute one command shape with many value sets without hiding driver capabilities.
- [Data representations and value fidelity](https://clickin.github.io/SQLBraid/v/1.0.0/concepts/data-representation.md): Preserve database value semantics at the driver boundary, then choose application types with Standard Schema.
- [Dynamic @braid directives](https://clickin.github.io/SQLBraid/v/1.0.0/concepts/dynamic-braid.md): Keep conditional SQL next to the statement while preserving lazy evaluation.
- [Parameter type hints](https://clickin.github.io/SQLBraid/v/1.0.0/concepts/parameter-hints.md): Choose an explicit database parameter type when driver inference is not enough.
- [Standard Schema result mapping](https://clickin.github.io/SQLBraid/v/1.0.0/concepts/result-mapping.md): Validate and transform rows without coupling SQLBraid to one schema library.
- [Routine calls](https://clickin.github.io/SQLBraid/v/1.0.0/concepts/routines.md): Author stored-procedure calls with explicit output, return, and heterogeneous result-set contracts.
- [Safe binds](https://clickin.github.io/SQLBraid/v/1.0.0/concepts/safe-binds.md): Keep values as driver parameters and make structural SQL explicit.
- [SQL tags and result kinds](https://clickin.github.io/SQLBraid/v/1.0.0/concepts/sql-tags.md): Declare what a SQLBraid statement returns without hiding the SQL.
- [Structural SQL fragments](https://clickin.github.io/SQLBraid/v/1.0.0/concepts/structural-fragments.md): Make identifiers, lists, joins, and trusted raw SQL visible in the API.

## Runtime
- [Direct connections and pools](https://clickin.github.io/SQLBraid/v/1.0.0/runtime/direct-pools.md): Choose the factory that matches your physical database resource.
- [Execution observers](https://clickin.github.io/SQLBraid/v/1.0.0/runtime/observers.md): Observe SQLBraid lifecycle events without coupling the runtime to a logger.
- [OpenTelemetry integration](https://clickin.github.io/SQLBraid/v/1.0.0/runtime/opentelemetry.md): Export SQLBraid database operation traces and duration metrics without coupling the runtime to an SDK.
- [Prepared queries](https://clickin.github.io/SQLBraid/v/1.0.0/runtime/prepared.md): Reuse a stable SQLBraid query shape without promising native driver preparation.
- [Streaming](https://clickin.github.io/SQLBraid/v/1.0.0/runtime/streaming.md): Iterate rows without buffering while SQLBraid owns the physical lease and driver cleanup.
- [Transaction option capabilities](https://clickin.github.io/SQLBraid/v/1.0.0/runtime/transaction-profiles.md): Fixed transaction options, physical scope, and driver evidence.
- [Transactions and savepoints](https://clickin.github.io/SQLBraid/v/1.0.0/runtime/transactions.md): Pin one physical connection and make transaction scope explicit.

## Metadata and code generation
- [codegen --check in CI](https://clickin.github.io/SQLBraid/v/1.0.0/metadata/ci.md): Keep generated models synchronized without editing derived files by hand.
- [Codegen configuration](https://clickin.github.io/SQLBraid/v/1.0.0/metadata/config.md): Generate deterministic TypeScript models from a metadata snapshot.
- [Inspectors and metadata snapshots](https://clickin.github.io/SQLBraid/v/1.0.0/metadata/inspectors.md): Capture database facts as validated, deterministic SQLBraid metadata.
- [Row, Insert, and Update models](https://clickin.github.io/SQLBraid/v/1.0.0/metadata/models.md): Understand the generated declarations and their conservative evidence rules.
- [Overrides and filters](https://clickin.github.io/SQLBraid/v/1.0.0/metadata/overrides.md): Narrow generated relations and resolve type evidence explicitly.

## Agents and editors
- [CLI inspect fallback](https://clickin.github.io/SQLBraid/v/1.0.0/agents/cli.md): Use bounded JSON inspection when an agent harness has no LSP client.
- [Driver-author binding guide](https://clickin.github.io/SQLBraid/v/1.0.0/agents/driver-author.md): Implement a custom SQLBraid adapter without crossing the value-only boundary.
- [Agent-native LSP](https://clickin.github.io/SQLBraid/v/1.0.0/agents/lsp.md): Use standard language-server protocol for SQLBraid evidence in coding agents.
- [Portable agent skill](https://clickin.github.io/SQLBraid/v/1.0.0/agents/skill.md): Install SQLBraid's application-development guidance in compatible coding agents.
- [VS Code extension](https://clickin.github.io/SQLBraid/v/1.0.0/agents/vscode.md): Use SQLBraid's thin TypeScript client without replacing built-in TypeScript support.

## Reference
- [Configuration](https://clickin.github.io/SQLBraid/v/1.0.0/reference/configuration.md): Configure codegen targets without adding runtime configuration dependencies.
- [Diagnostics and error codes](https://clickin.github.io/SQLBraid/v/1.0.0/reference/errors.md): Stable SQLBraid codes and the boundary each one protects.
- [Package map](https://clickin.github.io/SQLBraid/v/1.0.0/reference/packages.md): Find the SQLBraid package that owns each concern.
- [Runtime and driver support](https://clickin.github.io/SQLBraid/v/1.0.0/reference/support.md): Exact evidence, capability boundaries, and revision-specific support labels.
- [Troubleshooting](https://clickin.github.io/SQLBraid/v/1.0.0/reference/troubleshooting.md): Resolve the most common setup and runtime boundary mistakes.

## Release
- [Current limitations](https://clickin.github.io/SQLBraid/v/1.0.0/release/limitations.md): Know what the 1.0.0 GA contract deliberately does not promise.
- [1.0.0 release notes](https://clickin.github.io/SQLBraid/v/1.0.0/release/notes.md): The SQLBraid 1.0.0 GA contract and its capability and evidence boundaries.
- [Roadmap](https://clickin.github.io/SQLBraid/v/1.0.0/release/roadmap.md): Separate current behavior from candidates that need their own design and evidence.

## Optional
- [Interactive browser preview](https://clickin.github.io/SQLBraid/v/1.0.0/interactive-preview.md): Edit and run real SQL against a disposable SQLite WASM database in your browser.
